conventions.convention: Use T=(R/Z)^r and the product of right Milnor circle models. The Borel quotient uses (e,x)·t=(e·t,t⁻¹·x), with ordinary quotient topology.
Coefficients are Q or R. Each coordinate generator u_i has degree two and is c₁ of the associated coordinate-character line, identified with the tautological line rather than its dual.
The denominator set contains 1 and finite products of first Chern classes of nontrivial integral characters. It excludes zero; for r=0 it is {1}.

For the normal complex structure, pair inverse characters and retain the member whose first nonzero integer coordinate is positive. Euler classes use the resulting componentwise complex orientation; a rank-zero normal bundle has Euler class 1.

Localization applies here to compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifolds without boundary and ordinary Borel singular cohomology. No noncompact or compact-support conclusion is asserted.
Strong convexity means uniqueness of the globally length-minimizing affine geodesic, containment of its image, and smooth endpoint dependence. Empty manifolds and empty nerves are allowed.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, for k∈{Q,R}, define H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET×_T X;k), A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k), and the fraction localization at the multiplicative set generated by first Chern classes of nontrivial smooth characters.

Under countable choice, a smooth action of a product torus on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary admits an invariant metric. Its fixed set is a compact embedded smooth submanifold with finitely many components, tangent spaces equal to the fixed tangent subspaces, and normal bundle decomposing componentwise into nontrivial weights with constant multiplicities and an invariant complex orientation.

Under countable choice, for a smooth torus action on compact finite-dimensional boundaryless M with invariant metric, every compact embedded invariant submanifold has an equivariant normal exponential disk neighborhood. An orbit with stabilizer H has a tube T×_H Dε(V), and every stabilizer in that tube is contained in H.

Under AC, the product Milnor model for T=(R/Z)^r has BT≅(CP∞)^r and H^*(BT;Q)=Q[u₁,…,u_r]. Smooth characters correspond uniquely to integer vectors n, their associated lines have c₁=Σn_i u_i, and H_q(BT;k) is finite-dimensional in every degree for k=Q or R.

Under AC, for a smooth product-torus action on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable manifold without boundary, and k∈{Q,R}, character-localized Borel cohomology of M∖M^T is zero; equivalently, every class is annihilated by some finite product of nontrivial character classes.

Under AC, for the stated compact smooth torus action and k∈{Q,R}, the Euler class of the Borel normal bundle of F=M^T, in the supplied componentwise complex orientation, is a unit after character localization. Its restriction over a point of a fixed component is the product of its nontrivial normal character classes with multiplicity.

Under AC, a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth boundaryless Riemannian manifold F has a finite CW homotopy model and some N≥1 with H^q(F;k)=0 for q≥N, for every field k. Its positive-degree cohomology ideal therefore satisfies J^N=0.
For a commutative unital ring R, a multiplicative subset S containing 1 and excluding 0, and an exact sequence 0→M′→M→M″→0 of R-modules, the sequence obtained by fraction localization at S is exact.

Under AC, for a smooth action of T=(R/Z)^r on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold M without boundary and k∈{Q,R}, restriction to F=M^T induces a graded-ring isomorphism after localization at the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters.

concerns.concern: The Example and Verification Given do not assume AC, although the localization definition and theorem used in F1/F3 explicitly assume it. Carry that hypothesis into the example's public claim. F1 also says the real interface is 'conditional' because of a 'fresh-readiness-record gap', while the displayed Example asserts both coefficient cases without that qualification. This workflow-status caveat needs reconciliation with the actual mathematical premises.

The Example omits the AC hypothesis inherited by its cited Milnor/localization suppliers. F3 additionally calls the real coefficient interface 'conditional' because a readiness record is missing, while the Example states the real conclusion unconditionally. State the inherited assumptions consistently and separate workflow status from mathematical premises.

F2 asserts H^*(CP¹;k)=k[b]/(b²) citing the infinite-projective-space lemma and coefficient UCT. Cite and declare that supplier directly rather than leaving the finite-stage inference implicit. seams_checked.note: The opened coefficient lemma and Borel definition use the same product right Milnor model, period-one presentation and tautological real generators. The rational extension is proved locally; no Borel–Cartan comparison is assumed.

ABBV conventions use the same character denominators and right quotient. The theorem's L2 accurately states the compact boundaryless real Borel restriction isomorphism; its proof uses precisely that isomorphism.

The current index theorem uses the separate compact-symbol fixed-inclusion supplier, rather than claiming that Borel localization proves representation-ring localization. The indirect geometric use passes through the symbol page's slice and tube constructions.

The Borel–Moore definition uses the rational product-torus coefficient and character calculation faithfully. Its noncompact concentration is separately supplied; it does not cite the compact Borel theorem as a noncompact theorem.

Compact invariant tubes are used in analytic embedding comparison.
